    Kronecker bricks of dimension at most |k| #

    For a set Λ ⊆ k of scalars, the Kronecker module T_Λ = (k^(Λ), k ⊕ k^(Λ); a, b) with a(c) = (0, c) and b(c) = (∑_λ c_λ, (λ c_λ)_λ) is a brick: an endomorphism (g, h) satisfies (λ - μ) g(e_μ)_λ = h(1, 0)_λ, which forces h(1, 0) to have no second component and g to be diagonal; the first component of b then makes g scalar. Its dimension is 1 + 2|Λ|.

    In terms of P¹, T_Λ is the Kronecker module of the sheaf O(∑_{λ ∈ Λ} λ) (rational functions with at most simple poles in Λ). This gives the Göbel–Simson bricks of every infinite dimension κ ≤ |k|, over any field.
